clue.text: Make concession, giving a tip on time in prison

indicators.note: a tip on time means the tip piece is placed after the prison piece

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
taken as written
a point is a tip, as of a pencil or a knife

explanation.surface: Someone yields ground, offering a helpful hint about serving a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link; 'tip' looks like advice but is a sharp end.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a point is an idiom for allowing something beyond what the rules strictly permit, a concession.

clue.text: Things are much the same with this coin collection

definitions.text: Things are much the same with this

explanation.surface: A joke that a coin collection hardly alters things.
explanation.definitionFit: Small change is loose coins, and also something that makes little difference.

clue.text: Watch over terms of reference

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a timer is a watch or clock

explanation.surface: Someone supervises a committee's terms of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the set of instructions or area of authority given to someone.

clue.text: Upset salesman liable to pose questions

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the whole run reads from bottom to top

parts.note: REP, a representative, is a salesman
apt means liable or inclined
to set a question is to pose it

explanation.surface: An upset salesman is likely to start asking awkward questions.
explanation.walkthrough: REP + APT + SET gives REPAPTSET; 'Upset' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: A test paper is a printed set of exam questions.

clue.text: More husky rowers accommodated by lady

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed inside the lady piece

parts.note: her is a lady, referred to as her
oars stands for rowers, as in crew members

explanation.surface: A lady puts up a team of rowers with gruff voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarser means rougher-voiced, the sense of husky.

clue.text: Latin-American relieved of his anxiety

indicators.note: relieved of means the following word is taken away

parts.note: Hispanic describes someone of Latin-American descent

explanation.surface: A Latin-American is freed from his worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a strong form of anxiety.

clue.text: Frightened, I had turned out to have given a hint

indicators.note: turned out means thrown out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: intimidated means frightened or cowed
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A scared person turned out to have dropped a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like a phrase meaning proved, but here it ejects ID from INTIMIDATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest indirectly, so intimated means hinted.

clue.text: Over the odds, often from the start

indicators.note: from the start means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Remarks that a price is often excessive right from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the odds' looks like the definition, but only 'Over' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means excessively, as does over in words like overcautious.

clue.text: Agricultural building at a great distance —- a mile

parts.note: far means a long way off
M is the standard abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A farm building stands far off, about a mile away.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm is an agricultural establishment, here loosely called a building.

clue.text: Nothing much happens in this race for men only

indicators.note: the clue order is reversed here: the answer begins with the men-only piece and ends with the race piece

parts.note: a stag party or stag night is for men only
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A race open only to male competitors is described as uneventful.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs STAG then NATION, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of inactivity in which nothing develops, as in a sluggish economy.

clue.text: Australian egg-producer provides a supply that's irregular — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the time letter
irregular letters are out of order, so the words a supply are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated note that an Australian supplier finally delivers eggs, though erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's irregular' rearranges A SUPPLY into PLAYPUS; 'about' puts that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is a mammal of Australia that famously lays eggs.

clue.text: Manage to acquire pass

explanation.surface: Someone manages to pick something up while passing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to obtain something and, informally, to drop in or pass by.

clue.text: Support at home again set up without a problem

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
in means at home

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed word surrounds the a
up in a down clue means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: reset means set again

explanation.surface: A support at home was set up again without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RESET into TESER; 'without' wraps that round A to make TEASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainteaser is a puzzle or problem requiring thought.

clue.text: Kind of insurance for Liberal Democrats?

explanation.surface: A wry question about what insurance policy a British political party would take out.
explanation.walkthrough: Insurance covering claims by others is named for the outside party; the Liberal Democrats were long Britain's third-largest political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names cover for claims by others and, here, the third-largest British party.

clue.text: Disgruntled nurse felt bitter

indicators.note: bitter signals the letters are soured and churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A disgruntled nurse felt resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful means feeling aggrieved, which disgruntled also expresses.

clue.text: Gone rusty? It would be unusual for him

definitions.text: Gone rusty? It would be unusual for him

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are in an unusual order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Being out of practice would be rare for a youthful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges GONE RUSTY; the whole clue is the definition, since a young person seldom gets rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, unlikely to be out of practice or rusty.

clue.text: Contemptible person given a kicking, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: toed means kicked with the toe

explanation.surface: Someone despicable gets kicked, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a crossword and everyday insult for a loathsome person.

clue.text: Bishop freed from unexpected extra responsibility

indicators.note: freed from means the bishop letter is removed

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment or benefit
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman is relieved of an unexpected extra duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus means a burden or duty, a responsibility.

clue.text: Booming out in rude song

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud voice belting out a vulgar song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the ten letters of IN RUDE SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Resounding means echoing loudly, the same as booming.

clue.text: This can produce brown paper to wrap round maltreated head

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: round means the wrap piece goes around the next letter

parts.note: to lap is to wrap or enfold

indicators.note: head means the first letter of maltreated

explanation.surface: Brown paper is used to wrap round a badly treated head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown paper' looks like a unit, but 'brown' ends the definition; a sunlamp gives a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp emits ultraviolet light that can give skin a tan.

clue.text: Fresh meat -— sailors tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: veal is calf meat
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors tuck into a meal of fresh meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means of the spring, and so fresh and youthful.

clue.text: Discover king is superior to knight

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed above, so the king piece comes first

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's King Lear
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Finding that a king outranks a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to find out or discover.

clue.text: Point, say, made by the foreign officer that's rejected informal attire

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
eg, for example, is what say means
il is Italian for the
GEN is the abbreviation for general, an officer

explanation.surface: A foreign officer rejects someone's informal dress code.
explanation.walkthrough: E + EG + IL + GEN gives EEGILGEN; 'that's rejected' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light dressing gown, casual wear for the bedroom.

clue.text: South American gets home about noon

parts.note: in means at home
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A South American arrives home around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan means of the Inca people of Peru, so a South American.

clue.text: A man felt as bad as criminal

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are in a poor state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A man feels as wicked as a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges A MAN FELT AS; the second 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malfeasant describes someone doing wrong, especially an official committing an illegal act.

clue.text: A ship displaying a jack

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel flies a jack flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jack' suggests a flag but is a male donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a male donkey, and an ass is a donkey.

clue.text: Dative, perhaps, is an example

explanation.surface: A grammar note that the dative serves as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case; a case is also an instance or example.

clue.text: Dummy? He has no say

explanation.surface: A question about a mannequin answered by its silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy, in bridge or business, takes no active part, as does a partner with no say in running a firm.
